inputs.wacc_rationale: AUD-domestic, regulated-adjacent infrastructure telco with high revenue visibility (mobile oligopoly, contracted nbn Definitive Agreement receipts, tower leases). House AUD WACC ~7.5%, below the AU industrial-cyclical default (~9%, ORI.AX) and close to REIT/infra-grade names (APA.AX ~7%) given Telstra's scale, oligopoly market structure (3-player, ~40-44% mobile share) and contracted infrastructure income. Built from AUD risk-free ~4.3% (10yr ACGB) + levered equity risk premium, blended toward the company's own low cost of debt (A- rated, cost of debt ~4.5-5%) given ~35-40% gearing.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A) -- leases as debt. Telstra's own published net-debt definition is 'total lease liabilities, borrowings and derivative financial instruments, less cash' (FY2026 10-K note 4.4: borrowings $15,512m + lease liabilities $3,091m - net derivative assets $199m - cash $1,103m = net debt $17,301m). Lease principal is NOT deducted from the flows (AASB16 books lease principal repayments in financing activities, only lease interest sits in operating cash flow, so reported OCF/FCF already exclude lease-principal drag). Lease liabilities are carried inside total_debt/net_debt instead. D&A used for the EBIT/cash-tax build is total D&A ($4,839m FY26, includes $577m right-of-use depreciation) since the lease asset's economic consumption is a real cost and no lease charge is separately expensed in the FCF build -- this avoids double-charging the lease (no separate lease_cost_pct_path line is used).
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are attributable-only via a leakage rate folded into the cash_tax_rate_path (the engine has no standalone NCI driver, so NCI is charged once by combining it with the statutory tax rate: combined_rate = 1-(1-tax)*(1-nci_leakage), applied as the effective 'cash_tax_rate_path' in every scenario -- 35.25% base (30% tax, 7.5% NCI leakage), 34.9% bull (30% tax, 7.0% leakage), 35.6% bear (30% tax, 8.0% leakage)). No separate NCI deduction is taken in the net-debt/equity bridge, which avoids double-counting. FY2024-26 NCI profit share (Telstra PM Pty Ltd / Amplitel 49% minority plus other controlled entities) was $166m/$171m/$165m against total group profit of $1,788m/$2,343m/$2,406m = 9.3%/7.3%/6.9%, averaging ~7.8% and trending down as Telstra's own segments outgrow the Amplitel/PM minority slice; 7.5% used as the base-case leakage rate (flat across the path -- no evidence of a structural shift). Calibration check: FY0 NOPAT built from EBIT less the combined rate should approximate reported attributable net income of $2,241m within non-operating noise (net finance costs and other one-offs sit outside NOPAT in this component build).
inputs.notes: Routed via .claude/skills/dcf-methods/SKILL.md as an operating company, non-US/cyclical-adjacent row: owner-FCF DCF + references/owner-fcf-adaptations.md (leases, NCI). Telstra is a mature, low-growth (flat 10yr revenue CAGR, -1.2%) AUD integrated telco with growing high-margin infrastructure income (InfraCo Fixed nbn Definitive Agreement receipts, 51%-owned Amplitel towers) offsetting structurally declining Fixed Enterprise/International/legacy voice. FY2024 CapEx ($5,064m, 22.1% of revenue) includes a ~$2.8bn one-off spectrum payment -- normalized out of the base-year capex assumption; BAU capex in other years runs ~15-17% of revenue, matching FY27 guidance (BAU capex $3.35-3.65bn + strategic investment $0.2-0.3bn on $22.9bn FY26 revenue = ~15.5-17.2%). 10-year horizon used because underlying EBITDAaL margin (35.6% on total income) and the FY30 Connected Future 30 ambition (10% underlying ROIC, up from 9.0% FY26; mid-single-digit cash-earnings CAGR) imply margin is still maturing, not flat, over a 5-year window. July 2026 nationwide network outage (Triple Zero failures, Senate inquiry recommending Telstra lose control of the emergency call service, ACMA investigation with potential fines up to A$30m and possible Federal Court action, published 3-Sep-2026) is charged through the flows/scenario weighting per section 7f of the adaptations file (risk charged once, not stacked as a WACC premium): bear weight raised to 30% (from the 15% house default) and the bear case models sustained regulatory/reputational overhang -- elevated opex from remediation and compliance, ARPU/brand pressure, and a token A$30m fine impact via the equity bridge -- rather than a discount-rate adjustment. SBC is negligible (<0.15% of revenue); house and street bases are close to converging. Shares outstanding taken from the FY2026 annual report cover-page disclosure (11,139,136,247 shares on issue at 30 June 2026), not the CSV's derived (profit/EPS) FY2026 figure of ~11,261m -- the disclosed count is more precise and reflects the FY2026 buyback completion (245.9m shares repurchased and cancelled during the year).

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: blended: revenue is structurally near-flat (mobile ARPU growth and infrastructure monetisation offsetting declining Fixed Enterprise/International/legacy voice -- 10yr CAGR -1.2%, 3yr +0.3%), so the primary growth engine is margin expansion (positive operating leverage) and buybacks reducing the share count's economic claim, not top-line growth. Selected 2.0% as the base-case terminal-adjacent revenue growth rate, below both the equity and FCF CAGRs (both distorted -- equity by buybacks/Amplitel NCI carve-out in FY2023, FCF by the FY2024 spectrum spike and FY2024-25 volatility) and consistent with the low-single-digit revenue growth implied by FY27 guidance (underlying EBITDAaL guided 1.9-5.5% growth on roughly flat revenue).
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-0.4% to -5.6%) diverges sharply from EPS CAGR (+5-6%) and FCF 3yr CAGR (+7.5%) -- driven by capital return (buybacks reducing the equity base while EPS/cash-earnings grow) and the FY2023 Amplitel-related NCI reclassification (~$2.4bn of equity moved to non-controlling interests from FY2023), not by any deterioration in the underlying business. Equity CAGR is not used as the growth anchor for this reason; see growth_rate_source.

base.narrative: Base case: Connected Future 30 delivers as guided. Mobile ARPU growth and Network-as-a-Product initiatives keep mobile EBITDA growing low-to-mid single digits; InfraCo Fixed (nbn Definitive Agreement CPI-linked receipts) and Amplitel tower leasing keep growing at a high margin; declining Fixed Enterprise/International/legacy voice continues to shrink but its drag on group EBITDA fades as the mix shifts. Positive operating leverage (income growth > cost growth) pushes underlying EBITDAaL margin from 38.5% toward ~39.8% by year 5, consistent with the FY30 ambition of 10% underlying ROIC (up from 9.0% FY26). BAU capex intensity gradually eases from ~16% toward ~15% of revenue as the network-build phase of Connected Future 30 matures. The July 2026 outage produces a manageable regulatory outcome -- fines in the guided ACMA range (up to $30m), completed network resilience remediation, and no loss of the Triple Zero contract -- with no lasting impact on customer churn or brand.

bull.narrative: Bull case: digital-infrastructure monetisation (Aura intercity fibre, subsea cable capacity, satellite ground stations, further third-party Amplitel tower leasing to Optus/TPG) rides the AI/data-centre capex supercycle harder and faster than guided, and premium mobile ARPU growth continues even through cost-of-living pressure given Telstra's 8-time 'Best in Test' network quality edge. Cost-out and AI-enabled customer service (MyTelstra AI Assistant) push operating leverage above the FY30 10% ROIC target, reaching underlying EBITDAaL margin ~42% by year 5. Regulatory overhang from the July 2026 outage resolves quickly and cheaply (fine well inside the guided range, no forced divestment of Triple Zero control) and becomes a non-event for the multiple within 12-18 months. NCI leakage stays a touch lower as Amplitel's growth is increasingly driven by external (non-Telstra) tower tenants who pay Telstra's InfraCo/retail arm directly rather than diluting the Amplitel JV economics.

bear.narrative: Bear case: the July 2026 outage produces a sustained regulatory and reputational overhang -- ACMA fines toward the top of the guided $30m range plus Federal Court action, legislated loss of Triple Zero control (as the Senate inquiry recommended), and an external-review-driven remediation programme that keeps opex elevated for several years without a matching revenue benefit, compressing EBITDA margin back to ~36.5-37% and delaying the FY30 10% ROIC ambition. Brand damage and the Optus-TPG MOCN network-sharing agreement erode Telstra's network-quality pricing power, softening mobile ARPU growth into flat-to-slightly-negative in the first two years. Legacy Fixed Enterprise/International/NAS decline outpaces cost-out, and management's aggressive, partly debt-funded buyback programme (alongside a FY26 dividend payout ratio of 106% of statutory EPS) leaves less balance-sheet flexibility to absorb the combination of fine costs, remediation capex and softer earnings -- capex intensity rises rather than falls as network resilience investment is forced through. WACC held at the same 7.5% as base (risk is charged in the flows via the bear scenario and its 30% weight, not stacked again in the discount rate); terminal growth and the exit cap are both trimmed to reflect a structurally slower, higher-cost-base telco.

equity_bridge.item: ACMA outage-related fine provision (bear-case token estimate)
equity_bridge.note: Bear scenario only in spirit -- applied uniformly here as a conservative haircut since the engine applies one equity bridge across scenarios; ACMA investigation report published 3-Sep-2026 flagged potential fines up to A$30m plus possible Federal Court action (TLS.AX_Analysis.json risk register)

scenario_narratives.base: Connected Future 30 delivers roughly as guided: flat-to-low-single-digit revenue (mobile ARPU growth offsetting legacy decline), underlying EBITDAaL margin expanding from 38.5% toward ~39.8% on positive operating leverage, BAU capex easing from ~16% to ~15% of revenue, and the July 2026 outage resolving as a manageable, guided-range regulatory outcome.
scenario_narratives.bull: Digital-infrastructure monetisation (Aura fibre, subsea cable, satellite, Amplitel third-party tower leasing) rides the AI/data-centre capex supercycle faster than guided, mobile ARPU growth holds up on network-quality pricing power, and the outage overhang resolves quickly and cheaply -- margin reaches ~42% by year 5, ahead of the FY30 10% ROIC ambition.
scenario_narratives.bear: The July 2026 outage triggers sustained regulatory/reputational damage -- top-of-range ACMA fines, Federal Court action, legislated loss of Triple Zero control, and a multi-year remediation programme that keeps opex and capex elevated while brand damage and intensifying MOCN network-sharing competition soften mobile ARPU and revenue growth; margin stalls around 36.5-37.5% and the FY30 ROIC ambition slips.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default is 15/50/35 bear/base/bull. Bear weight raised to 30% (from 15%) because of the live, unresolved regulatory overhang from the July 2026 nationwide outage -- an ACMA investigation with potential fines and Federal Court action (report published 3-Sep-2026, days before this valuation), a Senate inquiry recommending Telstra lose control of the Triple Zero emergency call service, and elevated execution risk from running network-resilience remediation alongside the already-ambitious Connected Future 30 transformation simultaneously. Bull weight cut to 20% (from 35%) because the bull case requires several things to go right at once (faster-than-guided infrastructure monetisation AND a clean, fast regulatory resolution AND sustained ARPU pricing power against intensifying MOCN competition) while the base case already embeds continued execution of guided targets.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Telstra is Australia's dominant integrated telco -- a mature, structurally low-growth revenue base (flat-to-negative over 10 years) increasingly monetised through margin expansion, capital discipline (buybacks, progressive dividends) and a growing, high-margin, contracted digital-infrastructure income stream (InfraCo Fixed nbn payments, 51%-owned Amplitel towers, Aura fibre, subsea cable, satellite). The house owner-FCF DCF values the consolidated cash-generative core net of the Amplitel/PM minority interest (charged once via a ~7.5% NOPAT leakage rate) and net of total debt inclusive of lease liabilities (Telstra's own net-debt definition). The July 2026 nationwide outage and its regulatory fallout (ACMA investigation, Senate inquiry recommending loss of Triple Zero control) is a live, unresolved risk priced through an elevated 30% bear-case weight and a bear-case narrative of sustained opex/capex drag and slower ARPU growth, not through a WACC premium -- risk is charged once, in the flows.
key_risks_to_valuation: July 2026 outage regulatory outcome (ACMA fines/Federal Court action, potential loss of Triple Zero control) remains unresolved at valuation date and could be materially worse or better than the bear/base cases assume
Structural decline in Fixed Enterprise/International/legacy voice segments outpacing cost-out and infrastructure-income growth
Intensifying wholesale/infrastructure-sharing competition (Optus-TPG MOCN agreement) eroding Telstra's network-quality pricing advantage
Debt-funded buyback pace against a high (106% FY26) dividend payout ratio reduces balance-sheet flexibility if earnings or the regulatory outcome disappoint
Execution risk on the simultaneous, interdependent Connected Future 30 transformation programs (network evolution, digital infrastructure build-out, AI enablement)
